header: The calculator of the search bar. I wrote it as a small hand-made parser: it never calls eval or Function, so what a user types can only ever be arithmetic. Pure: no I/O, no model, nothing is stored or sent anywhere. Understands: + - * / ^ (and ** × ÷), brackets, "%" the way a pocket calculator does (200 + 10% = 220, 200 - 10% = 180, 200 * 10% = 20), "15% of 2400", Indian number words (5 lakh, 1.2 crore, 3 thousand) and 5k, Indian digit grouping (1,00,000), constants pi and e, and the usual functions. I keep the detector STRICT: the whole text must be arithmetic, with at least one operator or function. A date ("24-01-2026"), a year range ("2025-26"), a telephone-like number ("033-2345678"), a ticket number or any sentence is NOT an expression, and such text goes to the ordinary search untouched.

members.name: shown
doc: The expression as the parser understood it, tidied ("200 + 10%")

members.name: exact
doc: Set when the question was for a constant itself ("value of pi"); then I give its digits to full display length

symbols.name: Tok
symbols.sig: | { t: "num"; v: number } | { t: "op"; v: string } | { t: "id"; v: string }

symbols.name: FUNCS
symbols.sig: const FUNCS: Record<string, (x: number) => number> = { sqrt: Math.sqrt, cbrt: Math.cbrt, abs: Math.abs, round: Math.round, floor: Math.floor, ceil: Math.ceil, …

symbols.name: CONSTS
symbols.sig: const CONSTS: Record<string, number> = { pi: Math.PI, e: Math.E, phi: (1 + Math.sqrt(5)) / 2 }

symbols.name: MULTIPLIERS
symbols.sig: const MULTIPLIERS: Record<string, number> = { thousand: 1e3, k: 1e3, lakh: 1e5, lakhs: 1e5, lac: 1e5, lacs: 1e5, crore: 1e7, crores: 1e7, cr: 1e7, million: 1e6, mn: …

symbols.name: looksLikeNonMath
doc: I use this to catch text that only looks like arithmetic: dates, year ranges, telephone-like numbers.

members.name: used
doc: Set once an operator or a function was used: I do not count a lone number as a calculation

members.name: implicitTimes
doc: "2pi", "2(3+4)", "(1+1)pi", "pi 5": I read a number, bracket or constant straight before a constant, a function or an opening bracket as "times"; a number straight before a number is not.

symbols.name: SQRT_WORDS
doc: I accept roots and powers written as words: "sq rt of 4^3", "square root of 64", "cube root of 27", "5th root of 32", "square of 12", "cube of 3", "5 squared". After "of" I take the WHOLE rest as the argument ("square root of 16 + 9" is the root of 25), which the card shows back as "√(16 + 9)".

symbols.name: tidy
doc: I treat "what is", "calculate", "calc" and "=" around the arithmetic as noise and strip them; "15% of 2400" becomes "15% * 2400".

symbols.name: prettyShown
doc: I show the expression back on the card like this: roots as √ and ∛, simple squares and cubes as ² and ³.

symbols.name: constantQuestion
symbols.sig: function constantQuestion(raw: string): { name: "pi" | "e" | "phi"; shown: string } | null
doc: "pi", "π", "value of pi", "pi value", "what is e", "euler's number", "golden ratio", "φ": I answer with the constant itself, to full length. I do not take a lone "e" or a lone "phi" (a letter, a name people may type); "golden ratio" and the symbols π and φ I do take.

symbols.name: evaluateExpression
symbols.sig: export function evaluateExpression(raw: string): ExpressionResult | null
doc: Returns the value of an arithmetic expression, or null when the text is not one or cannot be evaluated (division by zero, an unknown word).

symbols.name: formatNumber
symbols.sig: export function formatNumber(v: number, sig = 10): string
doc: I group digits the Indian way: 1234567.891 -> "12,34,567.891". Up to 10 significant digits; very large or small values go in scientific form.

symbols.name: indianWords
symbols.sig: export function indianWords(v: number): string | null
doc: Gives the same value in Indian words when it is large: 12500000 -> "1.25 crore"; null below one lakh.

behaviours: plain arithmetic with precedence
power is right-associative and ** and ^ are the same
the multiplication and division signs
roots and powers written as words
root symbols and the whole rest after 'of' is the argument
roots are shown back with their symbol; a bare phrase or a sentence is not a calculation
pi and e: the constants themselves, to full length
the golden ratio: by name, by symbol, as a value question and inside sums
pi and e inside sums, with 'times' implied: 2*pi*8, 2pi, 2 pi 8, 4/3*pi*5^3, (1+1)pi, 3(4+5)
two numbers side by side are still not a product, and a letter without a value is not a calculation
percent as a pocket calculator reads it
'15% of 2400' and 'what is 15% of 2400'
a percent of a bracket is plain arithmetic, not a pocket-calculator percent
Indian number words and k
Indian digit grouping is read
constants and functions
a trailing = or ? and 'calculate' are ignored
scientific notation
a lone number, a lone percent or a bare word is not a calculation (a lone pi is a question for its value, tested above)
a date is not arithmetic
a year range is not arithmetic
a telephone-like or leading-zero number is not arithmetic
a sentence, a name, a site, a ticket are not arithmetic
an unknown word, division by zero, an open bracket and a stray character give nothing, never an error
nothing can run code: identifiers are only the listed functions and constants
a very long text is refused
deep brackets do not crash
huge results are refused, not shown as infinity
what was understood is shown tidied
Indian digit grouping in the result
floating-point dust is trimmed
very large and very small values use scientific form
a large value is also said in lakh and crore
